source: CPTS Module 03: Network Enumeration with Nmap
notes: -Pn skip host discovery, -n no DNS, --disable-arp-ping force IP probes. States: open, closed, filtered, unfiltered, open|filtered, closed|filtered.

references.title: HTB Academy - Network Enumeration with Nmap

name: Nmap - TCP Connect Scan & Port States
description: Full TCP connect scan (-sT) completes the handshake - useful without root or through proxies. --reason shows why Nmap labels a port open/filtered/closed.

defense.why_it_works: The TCP connect scan (-sT) completes the full three-way handshake through the OS socket API, so it needs no raw-packet privileges - but because the connection is fully established, the target service logs it, making it noisier than a SYN scan.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to the target (no elevated privileges required).
defense.impact: An open-port list obtained without raw-socket privileges.
defense.detection:
The TCP Connect scan (-sT) fully completes the three-way handshake, creating connection log entries on most systems and is easily detected by modern IDS/IPS solutions. The SYN scan (-sS) is more stealthy as it leaves the handshake incomplete, minimizing connection logs - but advanced IDS/IPS systems have adapted to detect even this subtler technique.

[MITRE T1046 AN1583] Monitor for execution of network enumeration utilities (nmap, netcat, net.exe, ping.exe, tracert.exe) in short succession, particularly when chained with lateral movement tools or system enumeration commands. [AN1584] Sequential ping, arp, or traceroute commands issued from bash scripts or interactive shells to map remote hosts are a strong behavioral indicator.
defense.artifacts: Fully established TCP connections logged by the target services and firewalls - noisier than a half-open SYN scan.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=network
| stats dc(dest_port) as ports dc(dest_ip) as hosts by src_ip, bin(_time, 1m)
| where ports>15 OR hosts>25

index=suricata event_type=alert alert.signature="*scan*"
| table _time, src_ip, dest_ip
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| summarize ports=dcount(RemotePort), hosts=dcount(RemoteIP), conns=count() by LocalIP, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where ports > 15 or hosts > 25
| sort by ports desc
// nmap -sT full TCP connect scan (completes 3-way handshake)
defense.sigma_rules: net_port_scan_activity (nmap -sT full TCP connect scan (completes 3-way handshake))
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1046 M1042] Disable or remove unnecessary services and functionality that expose attack surface. [M1030] Implement network segmentation to limit the set of hosts reachable from any given compromised system. Use firewalls to restrict which source addresses can reach each service port.
defense.evasion: Prefer the SYN scan (-sS) over Connect scan to reduce log entries. Advanced IDS/IPS will still detect SYN scans through pattern matching.
defense.misconfiguration: Network perimeters that do not filter ICMP, do not use egress filtering, or expose unnecessary services (all ports open) allow comprehensive port scanning. Systems without host-based firewalls or IDS/IPS allow scan traffic to enumerate every open service, revealing attack surface. No rate-limiting on inbound probes means stealth scans complete quickly.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# No firewall between attacker and target (or overly permissive rules):
# iptables -L  ->  Chain INPUT (policy ACCEPT)  [no rules]
# Or: Windows Firewall disabled
# Every service's port is reachable from any source

# No IDS/IPS:
# Snort/Suricata not deployed; no AWS GuardDuty / Azure Defender
# Nmap SYN scan completes in seconds with no alert generated
defense.secure_config:
# Linux host-based firewall - default-deny inbound:
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP
iptables -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
# Only open required services:
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT  # HTTPS only
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -s 10.10.1.0/24 -j ACCEPT  # SSH from mgmt network

# Rate-limit scan detection (drops SYN floods):
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --syn -m limit --limit 1/s --limit-burst 3 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --syn -j DROP

# Deploy IDS/IPS:
# Snort/Suricata rules detect nmap OS detection probes
# AWS: GuardDuty (detects port scans from EC2)
# Cloud: Security Groups default-deny with explicit allow rules

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, NetFlow / sFlow, Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Check for unusual network connections to/from the source host
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

variations.label: Packet-trace on a single port (diagnose closed/filtered state)

explain:
Completes the full TCP handshake to determine port state:
  -sT     TCP connect scan (works without root and through proxies)
  -p 443  the port
  -Pn -n --disable-arp-ping   no discovery/DNS/ARP
  --packet-trace              show the packets
  --reason                    print why Nmap calls a port open/closed/filtered
Use -sT when you cannot send raw packets (unprivileged, or over a SOCKS proxy).
